Subject: Re: Fwd: Private GPU pool sizing ask (Acme Payments)

Quick numbers and reasoning below (keeping it slide-friendly).

1) Starting provision recommendation (customer-facing):
- Target sustained QPS equivalent: 400 inference requests/sec (based on their CSV avg + 95th spikes mapped to model token counts).
- Model: quantized Llama2-13B-opt or similar (we recommended a ~13B-class because of quality/latency tradeoff).
- GPU type: 2x A10G per shard (or 1x A100S 80GB if they want fewer nodes but higher cost).
- Initial pool: 6 shards (12 A10G equivalent) to give ~12k tokens/sec aggregate (roughly maps to 400 req/s at avg token length), with room for autoscale to 9 shards for sustained growth.

Rationale: 6 shards gives ~25–30% headroom for the first quarter, supports concurrent warm sessions vs. cold startup. We assume batching efficiency of ~1.8x on their workload distribution.

2) Warm-pool & cache-warmup guidance:
- Warm pool size: keep ~30% of shards in warm standby (i.e., preloaded model weights and KV caches) to absorb short spikes within 20–40s.
- Cache warmup: full KV-cache populate for a hotspot prompt set takes ~2–4 minutes depending on seq length; recommend a pre-warm script to replay top 500 queries during maintenance windows.
- Fast path: canonical prefix caching for the common prompt templates (we can supply a script).

3) Network / jitter mitigations for Acme to validate on their side:
- Egress: ensure sustained egress >= 1.2 Gbps per 3-shard block during spikes; low sustained egress can cause packet pacing and increase tail latencies.
- MTU and intermittent MTU blackholes: confirm path MTU discovery; we saw fragmentation-induced jitter in their pcap on sub-1k payloads.
- TCP buffer sizing: increase socket buffers to avoid small-window stalls under burst.
- SYN/FIN bursts: if their client pool does many short connections, use connection pooling / keepalives to avoid TCP handshake jitter.

4) Operational handoff checklist (owners and runbook pointers):
- Infra (Acme): provision VPC cross-connect, egress quotas, route tables, and on-prem firewall exemptions for model shards.
- Redwood: provision pool, apply quantization profile, run warmup job, configure autoscale policy, and enable tracing.
- Joint: smoke test (50 concurrent sessions with ramp), report P50/P95/P99 latencies and token throughput.

Notes / open items:
- We need clarification on their retention windows (affects cache warmup cadence).
- Confirm whether they prefer fewer larger GPUs (A100S) vs more A10G for procurement pricing.

I'll draft a 1-slide summary for procurement and a short 30m technical review.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Great detail from Marissa — a few networking caveats to add that I asked Acme to confirm: 

- BGP flaps / route churn: if their SP has transient route updates under load, packet reordering can spike tail latency — recommend BGP dampening or multi-path testing.
- Egress QoS: ask them to set a high-priority class for inference egress to keep packets ahead of bulk backups.
- TCP pacing observed in pcap: suggests their client NICs may be using conservative pacing; ask for NIC firmware & kernel versions.
- Monitoring hooks: we should require passive tcp_lat_jitter and token_egress_rate metrics exported into our console for initial 72-hour onboarding.

Operationally, also recommend a blackbox test harness we drop into their VPC that can replay the pcap at line rate for validation — I'll attach the test harness instructions in the slide pack.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber | Networking & Edge, Redwood Inference

Hi Rajiv / Claire — thanks for the data and the pcap. Below is a concise plan you can pass to procurement and infra as a single-page summary; attached is the 1-slide summary and the short runbook.

Summary (1-paragraph):
Redwood recommends an initial private GPU pool sized to 6 shards (12 A10G-equivalent GPUs) with autoscale headroom to 9 shards. This configuration targets ~400 inference requests/sec sustained with P95 latency targets < 120ms for your fraud scoring model when using our recommended quantized 13B model profile. We will provision a warm-standby pool (~30% shards warm) and run a cache-warmup job during onboarding; network validation (egress >=1.2Gbps per 3-shard block, MTU validation, connection pooling) is required on your side. Redwood will own provisioning, warmup orchestration, and initial tracing; Acme infra will own VPC cross-connects, egress quotas, and firewall rules.

Mutual Action Plan (MAP):
- This week: Acme confirms egress cap and procurement preference (A10G vs A100S) and shares retention window. (Owner: Rajiv)
- Wed 24 Jun: 30m technical review (Redwood + Acme). (Owner: Dylan)
- Onboarding week: Redwood provisions pool, runs warmup scripts, and executes smoke test. (Owner: Marissa + Acme infra)
- 72-hour validation: joint report with P50/P95/P99 and token throughput; enable early autoscale if needed. (Owner: Jonas + Redwood ops)

Attachments: 1-slide procurement summary (slide deck), short runbook, and the pcap we received.

If acceptable, I'll book the 30m slot for Wed 24 Jun 10:00–10:30 PT. Please confirm.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Program Manager, Customer Onboarding — Redwood Inference
